correlation.rule: RequestId is present on every event. ExecutionId is present only for an admitted analysis attempt. RunId is present only after seal or on a stored-Run read. No event fabricates an identity for a lifecycle phase in which it does not exist.

volumeBudgets.rule: Budget ownership is phase-derived: RequestId before admission and for stored-Run reads; ExecutionId for an admitted attempt, including its post-seal projection. RunId may partition a post-seal stream but is never the only universal budget owner.
volumeBudgets.onExhaustion: Emit one typed truncation marker with omitted count/bytes and an exact retrieval route when retrieval exists.

producerOutput.rule: Producer stdout/stderr is captured, privacy-classed, bounded and attributed; it is never parsed as a public contract.

supportBundles.rule: User-triggered only, with a manifest of artifact IDs, privacy classes and redactions. No source bytes or resolved secret values by default.

truncation.rule: retrieval is a typed route or explicit unavailable; never absent.

assurance.rule: The allocation target and executable controls are specified. Checker success is architecture design-integrity evidence; no built host has been QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED.

authority.validationOwner: orchestration host RequestContext constructor and EventEnvelope validator
authority.callerRule: Public callers MUST NOT supply requestId. An optional caller correlation token is accepted only in a separately typed clientCorrelationId field, is untrusted display/audit metadata, and never aliases or replaces RequestId.
authority.propagationRule: After allocation, the immutable typed RequestContext is the only source of RequestId for events, host-audit records, and child operations. Sinks, providers, stages, profiles, and projection adapters cannot mint, replace, or accept a raw RequestId.

allocation.point: Immediately when a CLI/API/stored-view invocation crosses the first trusted host ingress, before request parsing, request validation, contribution/capability admission, project resolution, stored-Run lookup, event creation, ExecutionId allocation, or AttemptRecord creation.
allRequests: requests later rejected during parse or request-validation
allocation.analysisAttemptRule: RequestId allocation does not admit an attempt. Rejected requests have RequestId but no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, RunId, or Run. Stored-view requests have a new RequestId and the selected existing RunId but no new ExecutionId or Run.
allocation.entropyBoundary: Uses OS CSPRNG only as non-analysis host correlation metadata. RequestId is excluded from every analysis identity and semantic result, so this does not weaken the RESOLVED-INPUTS prohibition on entropy influencing analysis.

representation.raw: 16 uniformly random bytes from the OS CSPRNG
representation.decode: The 32 hexadecimal characters decode to exactly the 16 allocated bytes. Uppercase, padding, braces, UUID hyphens, alternate prefixes, empty values, or Unicode lookalikes are invalid rather than aliases.

collisionAndRetry.reservationRule: Before publishing RequestContext or any EventEnvelope, atomically reserve the candidate under a unique RequestId constraint. A host using durable audit/event custody reserves in the host request ledger transaction; an explicitly ephemeral invocation reserves in the process registry for its complete lifetime.
collisionAndRetry.onCollision: Discard the colliding candidate, draw a fresh independent 16-byte candidate, and retry atomic reservation. Never reuse the colliding candidate with a suffix or overwrite the existing request.
collisionAndRetry.onExhaustion: After eight colliding candidates, return typed host outcome REQUEST_ID_ALLOCATION_FAILED before request validation and before attempt admission; emit no ordinary EventEnvelope because no valid RequestId exists. Project it through requestIdContract.d9Projection.allocationFailure. This is an operational host failure, not a Run verdict and not a new public D9 code.
collisionAndRetry.externalRetry: Every new CLI invocation, API call, transport retry, or stored-view read is a new request and receives a new RequestId. RequestId is not an idempotency key. A mutation uses its separately typed mutationId; an internal retry that remains inside one accepted host request retains the same RequestContext and RequestId.
collisionAndRetry.collisionScope: Uniqueness is enforced over the registry's custody lifetime. A durable ledger never reissues an ID present in that ledger; an explicitly ephemeral process prevents duplicates among its live/retained-in-process requests.

d9Projection.rule: REQUEST_ID_ALLOCATION_FAILED is an internal typed cause projected through the existing D9 pre-admission host-I/O case. The trigger context is retained for diagnostics but does not extend D9's public axes, termination union, code vocabulary, or numeric exits.

custody.requestContext: Host-owned immutable value from successful reservation until every child operation and event sink closes.
custody.operationalRecords: May be retained in bounded progress/diagnostic/telemetry records and is required in HostAuditRecord. Retention follows the owning operational/audit plane, not analysis evidence custody.
custody.attemptLink: AttemptRecord may hold a non-semantic correlation link to RequestId outside the sealed Run manifest. The link cannot change SnapshotId, PlanId, facts, Coverage, findings, verdict, evidence, or Run identity.
custody.redaction: RequestId is opaque and contains no timestamp, project, user, path, or source content; it is still treated as correlation metadata in support bundles.

excludedFrom: Coverage, findings, verdict, policy and termination derivation
semanticExclusion.rule: Changing only RequestId while holding all semantic inputs and exact Coverage fixed cannot change SnapshotId, PlanId, any fact/finding identity, EvidenceDigest, RunId, Run content, verdict, or termination. RequestId may correlate operational records but never establishes evidence authority.

auditPlane.boundary: Outside the analysis EvidenceDigest; audit identity never changes an analysis result identity.
auditPlane.ordering: Monotonic sequence per ProjectId, allocated transactionally.
auditPlane.atomicity: No authoritative mutation becomes visible without a COMMITTED audit outcome in the same ledger transaction. Non-transactional external effects require a durable PREPARED record first and deterministic recovery.
auditPlane.failure: Failure to persist PREPARED refuses the mutation. A crash after an external effect leaves PREPARED/RECOVERY-REQUIRED, never an unaudited success.
auditPlane.redaction: Records contain typed IDs, commitments and secret handles; never resolved secret values or source excerpts.

HostAuditRecord.commitmentRule: A canonical typed object commitment or explicit null when no object exists; prose before/after values are invalid.

floatOrExponent.conversion: Validate grammar, significand digits, exponent digits, and exponent magnitude before float conversion; reject every nonfinite conversion result.

numericTokenPolicy.runtimeIndependenceRule: Every token is accepted or rejected by these declared bounds before an ambient runtime conversion limit can act. Parser refusal always produces the declared named CLI finding with no traceback.
